title: Certify four physical C5 cost floors by exact rational separation
body:
This gives exact rational separation certificates for the four physical C5 residuals left by PR3268 after PR3271. Every finite asymmetric strict-scalar fit over Q/R/C costs at least 20 under the complete-plane binary pairing tariff, and five explicit rank-four terms attain 20 on each core.

The distinct contribution is a linear certificate: after the necessary equality-trace constraints, each of 57 cases is separated even for **real nonnegative support multiplicities**. Acceptance checks integer inequalities; it needs no count-state search or numerical optimizer.

**Concurrent result:** Nick Petalas's #3279 (`67c1360a7a6e81bcac515c698d56656454340b10`) independently proves the same four-core conclusion by finite-state count closure. It appeared during this session's verification and is explicitly credited. This is a separately derived proof certificate, not a priority claim or a new headline bound beyond that concurrent theorem. Our [scoped investigation](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1587#discussioncomment-19003766) records the rational-separation method before publication.

The single isolated package `research/c5-four-residual-floors/` contains the written proof, compact certificates, two implementations, behavioral controls, pinned inputs and replay manifest. It changes no shared verifier or frozen source. Scientific base and refreshed canonical main: `463113d675af7410ac91d53a4fed51ec6494eb9a`, priority revision 6; task `coverage-law-change`, explicitly narrowed to the residual proof handoff.

Evidence:

- Registered CPython 3.12.12 replay passes: 4,096 actual pairing tariffs, all 57 slack cases, and 14,045 admissible-term inequalities.
- The separate implementation uses explicit bit vectors, dense binary elimination and affine graph trace propagation; it agrees with the primary packed-rank/Fraction-elimination implementation. Five separate terms each cost four on every core. Nine optimized unittest groups and the independent geometry/trace controls pass.
- All 11 final package/input byte comparisons and committed-export integrity pass at `a3a7306c15c7da541e4b586fdb642e2855fc2956`. The read-only Git-free export passes the three scripts on optimized CPython 3.14.6. Its tested scientific bytes are identical to this final commit; only README and CHECKS changed to add the concurrent result and evidence.
- The latest full overlap snapshot covers 323 open PRs, 2,630 closed/merged PRs and 2,115 Discussion records with complete pagination and no warnings; a supplementary live check found #3279. Arbitrary diffs and unpublished work remain outside this coverage.

```sh
python3.12 -W error -B scripts/research_package.py \
  --package research/c5-four-residual-floors
```

The result is local to four fixed physical cores and the inherited strict scalar mask/tariff. It is not a global 112-port floor, native supplier, full restoration/hosting/precision invoice, formal multiplication theorem or new kappa. No selected cold replay, proof-kernel verification or independent human review was run. The next substantive question is a valid global charging inequality without double-counting shared supports; no further search round is reserved.

Credit Nick Petalas/PR3268/PR3271/PR3279, thakrarsagar/PR3256 for the weighted-rank and equality-trace method, Tekalign/PR2782, Arham Tahir/PR2879, Sagar Thakrar/PR2484, Cinna Davis/PR1825, Adam Gall/PR1889, PR3232/PR3248, ctoth, Philippe Van Velzen and the retained E8/P112 lineage. Prepared by Krzysztof Wójt with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; the supporting Luna implementation is disclosed. Apache-2.0.
